variants.zero_padded_full: v1 add_low_rank on a b zero-padded to every column: the whole tensor is read and written
variants.zero_update_not_kept: an element whose terms are all zero is still computed, so (-0) + (+0) = +0
variants.low_rank_from_zero: s = +0 accumulated over k first, then w = add(widen(W), s)

cases.purpose: v1 case lr-tie-even-down with columns = every column: 1 + 2^-8 is a BF16 tie; the even neighbour is 1.0 (0x3f80)
v1 case lr-tie-even-up with columns = every column: 1 + 3*2^-8 is a BF16 tie; the even neighbour is 1 + 2^-6 (0x3f82)
v1 case lr-tie-negative with columns = every column: -(1 + 2^-8) ties to -1.0 (0xbf80)
v1 case lr-double-rne1 with columns = every column: 1 + 2^-8 + 2^-30: single RNE gives 0x3f81, f32 then BF16 gives 0x3f80
v1 case lr-double-rne2 with columns = every column: 1 + 2^-8 + 2^-30: single RNE gives 0x3f81, f32 then BF16 gives 0x3f80
v1 case lr-double-f32 with columns = every column: 1 + 2^-8 + 2^-30: the f32 sum is already 1 + 2^-8, a tie -> 0x3f80
v1 case lr-double-negative-rne2 with columns = every column: -(1 + 2^-8 + 2^-30) under the double chain gives 0xbf80
v1 case lr-from-w with columns = every column: w + a0b0 + 3 x 2^-54, sequential from w: each 2^-54 is lost; from zero it is not
v1 case lr-negzero-plus-poszero with columns = every column: (-0) + (+0) = +0
cases.differs_from_v1_because: elements whose terms are all zero keep a base -0 (v1 writes +0)

cases.purpose: v1 case lr-negzero-plus-negzero with columns = every column: (-0) + (-0) = -0, preserved as 0x8000
v1 case lr-tiny-negative with columns = every column: -2^-140 rounds to -0 in BF16 (0x8000)
v1 case lr-tiny-negative-rne2 with columns = every column: -2^-140 is an f32 subnormal, then -0 in BF16
v1 case lr-f32-step-subnormal with columns = every column: 2^-130 + 2^-140 is an f32 subnormal at the chain's f32 step
v1 case lr-bf16-subnormal with columns = every column: 3 x 2^-133 is a BF16 subnormal (0x0003)
v1 case lr-bf16-subnormal-tie with columns = every column: 2.5 x 2^-133 ties to 2 x 2^-133 (0x0002)
v1 case lr-subnormal-base-rne1 with columns = every column: a BF16-subnormal base (0x0003) widens exactly: + 2^-133 gives 0x0004
v1 case lr-subnormal-base-f32 with columns = every column: a BF16-subnormal base is an f32 subnormal under the f32 profile (DAZ)
v1 case lr-smallest-normal with columns = every column: 2^-126 - 2^-134 rounds up to the smallest normal (0x0080)
v1 case lr-f32-profile-subnormal with columns = every column: 3 x 2^-133, an f32 subnormal operand, under the f32 profile
v1 case lr-max-finite with columns = every column: the largest BF16 (0x7f7f) plus a quarter ulp (2^118) stays 0x7f7f
v1 case ref-overflow-rne1 with columns = every column: max BF16 + 2^119 is the tie above the largest BF16; ties-to-even overflows
v1 case ref-overflow-rne2 with columns = every column: max BF16 + 2^119: exact at the f32 step, overflows at the BF16 step
v1 case ref-overflow-f32-step with columns = every column: max BF16 + 2^126 is finite in f64, overflows at the f32 step
v1 case ref-intermediate-f64 with columns = every column: a*b = 2^1000 * 2^1000 overflows f64
v1 case ref-intermediate-f32 with columns = every column: under the f32 profile, 2^100 * 2^100 overflows f32
v1 case ref-inf-b with columns = every column: an infinite b
v1 case ref-nan-fixup with columns = every column: a fixup with NaN bits
v1 case ref-inf-fixup with columns = every column: a fixup with +inf bits
v1 case ref-overflow-f32-profile with columns = every column: f32 profile: max BF16 + 2^119 is exact in f32, a tie that overflows BF16
v1 case ref-nan-a with columns = every column: a NaN in a
v1 case ref-inf-base-low-rank with columns = every column: a -inf base element (add_low_rank touches every element)
v1 case ref-fixup-no-op-rne2 with columns = every column: under the double chain the computed value is 0x3f80, so this fixup is a no-op
v1 case lr-fixup-rne1 with columns = every column: the same fixup under the single chain is a real correction (0x3f81 -> 0x3f80)
v1 case ref-rank-zero with columns = every column: rank 0
v1 case ref-ab-size with columns = every column: b is not rank x cols
v1 case lr-general-rne1 with columns = every column: 16 x 6, rank 2, random operands
v1 case lr-general-rne2 with columns = every column: 16 x 6, rank 2, random operands
v1 case lr-general-f32 with columns = every column: 16 x 6, rank 2, random operands

the sham law: a = 0 over a tensor with -0 elements inside J leaves every byte of the tensor unchanged

K = 1, b[0] = 0 (column J[0] = 1): every element of that column keeps its bits, -0 included; column 3 is written
K = 2: term 0 is zero and term 1 is not, so the element is written; the zero term adds +0 and the result is the ordinary one
from -0: a nonzero update 2^-200 is written; w = -0 + 2^-200 rounds to +0 in BF16 (the sign of the value)
from -0: a nonzero update -2^-200 is written and rounds to -0
f32 profile: the product of two nonzero operands underflows to +0, so the element is written (written is decided on operands, not on rounded products): -0 becomes +0
terms +x and -x are nonzero operands, so the element is written: -0 + x = x, x + (-x) = +0, and the result is +0
+0 with a zero update stays +0
